analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: Public site traffic and sessions. Enable the Native Analytics plugin to start collecting data.
analytics.disabledBody: Enable the Native analytics plugin under Plugins to show this dashboard and the sidebar link.
analytics.liveUsersHint: Estimated active sessions on the public site right now.
analytics.noData: No data yet — start collecting via the analytics ingest endpoint.
analytics.sessionsSub: IP (masked), country, page, and time on page
analytics.tableFootnote: IP and durations are illustrative. Production data comes from your analytics ingest endpoint and server-side geo lookup.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.noRecentContent: No content yet. Create your first entry.

backup.heading: Backup & restore
backup.description: Export a JSON backup, import selective data, and manage recent snapshots. Extra verification is required before opening this section.
backup.mfaHint: Enter your account password to unlock backup operations for this session.
backup.exportIntro: Choose which areas to include in the downloadable JSON file. Data is fetched live from the API and database.
backup.importIntro: Select a backup JSON produced by this panel. Choose which sections to restore, then apply to the database via the API.
backup.recentEmpty: No backups yet. Create one to see it listed here and to re-download anytime.
backup.footerNote: Backups export live data from your API and database. Imports are written back to the database via the API.
backup.nothingSelected: Select at least one area to include.
backup.restoreNoSnapshots: This backup has no data to restore.
backup.restoreError: Could not read this backup file.
backup.invalidFile: Not a valid CMS backup JSON.
backup.importNothingApplied: No matching sections found in backup.

appearance.heading: Appearance Settings
appearance.description: Customize the look and feel of your CMS
appearance.panelLanguageHint: UI copy is loaded from JSON files in src/locales/ (e.g. en.json, tr.json). Edit those files or add a new locale and register it in src/app/i18n/catalog.ts to customize wording.

database.heading: Database
database.description: Choose SQLite or PostgreSQL, configure the connection, and manage schema migrations.
database.bannerBody: Values here are for documentation and UX. In production, set DATABASE_URL (or split vars) in your server environment and run migrations from your deploy pipeline.
database.sqliteDesc: Single file — ideal for local development and lightweight installs.
database.postgresDesc: Server database — recommended for production and horizontal scaling.
database.sqlitePathHint: Relative to the app root or an absolute path on the host.
database.pgSslSub: Enable for managed Postgres and cloud providers
database.migrationsDescription: Applied and pending schema revisions. Use your ORM or migration tool on the server; this list mirrors typical workflow.
database.runMigrationsSub: Runs pending Prisma migration files against the database.
database.savedDemo: Configuration displayed from API. Connection details are read-only (set via DATABASE_URL).

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Extend your CMS with optional features. Enable or configure each plugin below.
plugins.installedDescription: Plugins that ship with this workspace. Additional plugins can be added later.

cookie.name: Cookie Management
cookie.description: Show a consent banner, respect visitor preferences, and keep cookie categories in sync with your front-end.

gemini.name: Gemini API Auto Translate
gemini.description: Use Google Gemini to suggest or fill translations for content locales from the editor (configure your API key below).
gemini.apiKeyPlaceholder: Paste your key from Google AI Studio
gemini.apiKeyHint: API key is saved to the backend API. For extra security, use a server-side environment variable in production.
gemini.modelsEmpty: No suitable models returned for this key.
gemini.tokenCostFootnote: Token counts are approximate (~4 characters per token). USD is estimated from Google paid-tier Standard text rates for the selected model; free quota, Priority/Flex, and current prices may differ. See Google AI Studio for billed usage.
gemini.keyMissing: Add an API key to enable translation requests.

s3.name: S3-compatible bucket storage
s3.description: Connect media and asset uploads to an S3 API–compatible bucket. Pick a provider, then enter endpoint, credentials, and bucket. Settings are saved to the API.
s3.pathStyleHint: Often required for MinIO and some on-prem S3 gateways.
s3.credentialsMissing: Add bucket name and access keys so uploads can target your storage.
s3.endpointHint: Example for the selected provider — replace region or account placeholders with your values.
s3.storageHint: Credentials are saved to the API. Use IAM-scoped keys and server-side configuration in production.

sitemap.name: XML Sitemap
sitemap.description: Configure how published URLs are exposed in sitemap.xml for crawlers. Settings are saved to the API and the backend serves /sitemap.xml automatically.
sitemap.baseUrlHint: No trailing slash. Used to build absolute <loc> entries.
sitemap.baseUrlMissing: Set a valid http(s) base URL so sitemap entries can be resolved.
sitemap.includeDraftsHint: Usually off for production SEO; enable only for staging or preview sites.
sitemap.pingHint: Optional Google/Bing ping URLs — wire this on the server when content goes live.
sitemap.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API and synced across sessions. The backend serves the sitemap at /sitemap.xml.

robots.name: robots.txt editor
robots.description: Edit the crawl rules served at /robots.txt. The backend serves the saved content at your-domain/robots.txt.
robots.editorHint: Plain text, one directive per line where applicable. Comments start with #. Validate with your search console tools after deploy.
robots.contentMissing: Add at least one rule or comment so crawlers get explicit guidance.
robots.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. Your backend serves this content at /robots.txt with text/plain.

redis.name: Redis cache
redis.description: Point your API at Redis for response, fragment, or query caching. Settings here are for documentation and local preview — real connections must use server-side env vars in production.
redis.tlsHint: Enable for managed Redis with TLS termination (e.g. cloud providers).
redis.keyPrefixHint: Namespace keys so multiple apps can share one Redis instance safely.
redis.defaultTtlHint: Fallback expiry for cache entries when the API does not set one.
redis.connectionMissing: Set host, valid port (1–65535), and numeric DB index to describe your Redis endpoint.
redis.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. Redis connection details are stored server-side; never expose passwords in client-facing code.

smtp.name: SMTP mail
smtp.description: Send transactional mail through your SMTP server and choose when editors get alerts for new or updated content (wired on the server in production).
smtp.serverMissing: Set SMTP host, valid port, and a valid from email.
smtp.notifyIntro: Choose which content types and lifecycle events should trigger an email to your team.
smtp.recipientsHint: Separate multiple addresses with commas or semicolons.
smtp.recipientsMissing: Add at least one recipient email when alerts are enabled.
smtp.notifyOnDraftSavedLabel: When a draft is first saved (created)
smtp.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. Mail is sent from your backend using the configured SMTP credentials.

n8n.name: n8n automation
n8n.description: Forward CMS events to an n8n workflow webhook. Choose which actions n8n may react to and what the payload should include (wired on the server in production).
n8n.connectionIntro: Point the CMS at your n8n Webhook node URL. Use HTTPS only.
n8n.instanceUrlHint: For your team’s reference; outbound calls use the webhook URL below.
n8n.webhookUrlInvalid: Webhook URL must start with https://
n8n.signingSecretHint: If set, your backend can sign requests so n8n can verify authenticity.
n8n.triggersIntro: Select which CMS events should POST to your webhook when this integration is enabled server-side.
n8n.payloadIntro: Optional fields included in the JSON body sent to n8n.
n8n.payloadIncludeLocalesLabel: Include locale list / localized fields summary
n8n.webhookMissing: Set an HTTPS webhook URL so n8n can receive events.
n8n.triggersMissing: Enable at least one event type, or nothing will be sent to n8n.
n8n.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. Keep secrets in environment variables and send webhooks from the backend in production.
n8n.testWebhookDemoNoUrl: Save a valid https:// webhook URL first.

outboundWebhook.name: Outbound webhook
outboundWebhook.description: Send CMS events to any HTTPS endpoint — Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Zapier, Make, or your own service. Pick which notifications to forward (wired on the server in production).
outboundWebhook.connectionIntro: Paste the incoming webhook URL from your tool. Only HTTPS is accepted.
outboundWebhook.channelHint: Shown in logs and the admin UI only; it does not change how requests are sent.
outboundWebhook.signingSecretPlaceholder: Shared secret for HMAC or custom verification
outboundWebhook.signingSecretHint: Use in production so your receiver can verify payloads from the CMS backend.
outboundWebhook.triggersIntro: Choose which CMS events should trigger a POST to this URL when the integration runs server-side.
outboundWebhook.payloadIntro: Optional fields included in the request body.
outboundWebhook.payloadIncludeLocalesLabel: Include locale list / localized fields summary
outboundWebhook.webhookMissing: Set an HTTPS webhook URL for this channel.
outboundWebhook.triggersMissing: Select at least one event, or no notifications will be sent.
outboundWebhook.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. Configure webhook signing secrets on the server; never expose them in client code.
outboundWebhook.testWebhookDemoNoUrl: Enter a valid https:// webhook URL first.

nativeAnalytics.name: Native analytics
nativeAnalytics.description: Collect page views, time on page, and geo from your public frontend via a small SDK. Metrics appear in the Analytics screen when enabled.
nativeAnalytics.connectionIntro: Your backend should expose a POST URL that accepts JSON events from the browser SDK (see snippet below).
nativeAnalytics.ingestUrlInvalid: If set, ingest URL must start with https://
nativeAnalytics.siteKeyHint: Non-secret identifier sent with each event; validate on the server.
nativeAnalytics.siteKeyMissing: Add a public site key so the SDK and API can match requests to this project.
nativeAnalytics.sdkModuleHint: Module in this repo: src/app/analytics/wolentAnalyticsClient.ts — copy into your public site or import via monorepo path alias.
nativeAnalytics.sdkNote: Payload shape: { type: "pageview" | "heartbeat", siteKey, path, title?, referrer?, activeSeconds?, ts }. Implement validation and rate limits on your API.
nativeAnalytics.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. The analytics dashboard shows real pageview and session data from your backend.

imageOptimization.name: Image optimization
imageOptimization.description: Transcode raster uploads and API responses to WebP with sensible defaults: quality, max dimensions, metadata stripping, and optional responsive widths (applied on the server or worker in production).
imageOptimization.recommendedBody: WebP quality 82, max width 2560 px, strip metadata, auto-orient from EXIF, WebP effort 4, generate 480–1920 srcset variants, keep originals in cold storage. Adjust per brand if banding appears (raise quality) or CPU is tight (lower effort).
imageOptimization.webpDisabledHint: WebP delivery is off — re-enable to match the “all images as WebP” pipeline.
imageOptimization.qualityInvalid: WebP quality must be a number from 1 to 100.
imageOptimization.effortInvalid: WebP effort must be an integer from 0 (fast) to 6 (smallest files).
imageOptimization.dimensionInvalid: Max width/height must be empty or a pixel value from 1 to 16384.
imageOptimization.deliverAsWebpLabel: Deliver all raster images as WebP
imageOptimization.deliverAsWebpHint: JPEG/PNG uploads are transcoded; SVG and vector assets are unchanged. Public URLs and the media API should serve the optimized WebP variant.
imageOptimization.qualityHint: 80–85 is a good balance; use 75–78 for thumbnails if needed.
imageOptimization.effortHint: Higher = smaller files and more CPU. 4 is a solid default (Sharp / libvips style).
imageOptimization.maxDimHint: Empty = no limit on that axis. Downscale before encode to save bytes.
imageOptimization.stripMetadataLabel: Strip EXIF / IPTC / XMP (recommended for privacy & size)
imageOptimization.autoOrientLabel: Auto-orient using EXIF before stripping metadata
imageOptimization.retainOriginalsHint: Useful for re-processing later; delivery still uses WebP.
imageOptimization.srcsetWidthsHint: Example: 480,768,1200,1920 — your image CDN or worker emits one file per width.
imageOptimization.demoHint: Settings are saved to the API. The backend applies Sharp image processing automatically on every upload.

plugins.footer: More plugins and a marketplace will appear here as they become available.
